paragraphs.text: [Ya Shi Xiang](dancong:ya-shi-xiang), duck dung aroma, is the market name for one line of [Phoenix Dancong](dancong:definition), traced to Pingkengtou village. Most lists of the [ten aroma types](dancong:aromas) leave it out, though it sells widely. In 2014 the name Yinhua Xiang, silver flower aroma, was put forward for it, and many sellers keep the old one. Three stories explain that old name: that it was chosen to put thieves off the bush, that it comes from the yellow local soil called duck dung soil, and that duck droppings lay on the bush.

The leaf comes from [Phoenix Mountain](phoenix-mountain:where-it-is), Fenghuang Shan, the high ground of the Chaoshan region in eastern Guangdong, where tea grows from the foothills up to roughly 1,100 metres. [Cloud and mist](phoenix-mountain:mist-and-climate) sit on the upper slopes for much of the year and the nights are cool, so the bushes grow slowly, and the trade links that slow growth to a thick leaf.
This is a 2026 leaf. Freshly roasted Dancong is [rested for some months](dancong:ageing) before it is drunk, though how many is not agreed, and it keeps sealed, dry, cool and out of the light.

brewing.text: Brew it gongfu style in a small gaiwan or clay pot, with about 3 to 8 grams for 100 to 120 ml and hot water, about 88 to 100°C; Chinese accounts mostly say 95 to 100°C. A quick rinse is common. Steeps start at a few seconds and grow a few seconds each round, and a good Dancong gives about eight to fifteen. Too long, too hot or too much leaf and it turns bitter and astringent.

notice.text: Flowers above all, a sweetness that comes back after swallowing, a high scent that lasts, honey, often ripe fruit such as peach, and what the trade calls mountain rhyme, shan yun; a liquor from golden to orange-red or amber.

unsupported.sentence: Freshly roasted Dancong is rested for some months before it is drunk, though how many is not agreed, and it keeps sealed, dry, cool and out of the light.
unsupported.why: The claim (dancong:ageing) says the tea is rested for some months before it is at its best. That is about when it tastes best. The description says it is rested before it is drunk, which claims a practice of not drinking it until then. No claim says that.
